name: Samoa
headline: Samoa: +4.2% growth in 2025, 1.8% inflation, debt 21% of GDP
sections: Samoa is a $1.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 201st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.2% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $9,319 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 4.9% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 1.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 13.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 21% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 43% in 2020. The general government balance is +4.7% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +5.7% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 71% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 24% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 71.8 years (2024). Population: 212 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
